title: Lower glycolysis perturbations converge on OGT and nuclear-speckle markers in thalamic and hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Pgk1 knockdown in 151 TH repressed Pgk1, Pnisr, Rsrp1, Srrm2, Arglu1, Ogt, and Grm1 at FDR<0.05. Gapdh in the same class independently repressed Pnisr, Ttc14, Rsrp1, Ogt, and Leng8 at FDR<0.05, while Tpi1 was self-depleted in 151 TH and showed nominal 151 TH movement of Pnisr/Ttc14/Rsrp1 plus an FDR-supported Ogt decrease in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
biological_interpretation: Lower glycolysis perturbations in selected glutamatergic neurons couple metabolic stress to a compact Ogt and nuclear-speckle/RNA-processing state, but the effect is not shared by every glycolytic node.
caveats: Gapdh mRNA itself was absent from the measured features, and Tpi1 secondary rows in 151 TH were nominal rather than FDR-supported.
The relationship links transcriptomic readouts to glycolysis and O-GlcNAc biology but does not measure glycolytic flux, UDP-GlcNAc, or OGT activity.

prior_expectation.summary: GAPDH and PGK1 are adjacent cytosolic glycolysis enzymes; TPI1 catalyzes the DHAP/G3P step of glycolysis; PNISR, RSRP1, SRRM2, ARGLU1 and related readouts are annotated RNA-processing or spliceosome-associated proteins
